title: The Hunters Hunted
timelinePosition: Same night as Chapter 7, minutes after Sylvanas pinches out the candle at the militia post. Warm, dry night (Ch7: no wet streets; frost on Jaina's linen on a warm night). Scene 1 runs from the take in the back lane behind Kett's into Havel's nearby shelter (the safe house). Scene 2 is the flight through the granary district's back streets the same night and the arrival at Corin's hideout. Scene 3 is the hour after, in Corin's hideout, before first light, with the search ring still out.
openLocation: Andorhal granary district at night: the back lane behind Kett's granary off Tenter Row (long and straight, loading doors barred, a lamp at each end, no doorway deep enough to stand in; Kett's is the last door on the left). Then Havel's shelter off Hurdle Lane (the safe house), the back streets, and Corin's hideout.
transport: On foot through the city under cover and stealth. Horses are left in a carter's yard (Ch7).
immediateObjective: Take a living cultist, force the Andorhal cell to reveal who is above it, and get out before the city closes around them.
constraints: Limited third, absolute: Jaina only. Nothing she cannot see, hear, feel, read or infer. She senses magic and contamination; she cannot read Sylvanas's reasons, only the shape of the calls. Havel's guilt reaches her as pattern and body, not as a narrated fact, until the escape exposes it.

Address: narration says 'Sylvanas' (Ch4 onward); aloud Jaina says 'Ranger-General'. Lyriel calls her 'Jaina'; Cyndia does not. Sylvanas aloud says 'Mage', or 'Proudmoore' in front of others. No warm trust language; the partnership shows as coverage of blind sides, never speeches.

Jaina's body (carried Ch2-7): right hand dead, left raw with two usable fingertips. She cannot write. 'Emergency notes' in B6 and the map work in B7 MUST be Corin's hand at her dictation, or Jaina working from spoken memory and spell-light marks. Her spells cost her; she is depleted going into the night, and Ch7 set up a single jaw-freeze on the target that she can do only once tonight.
No dialogue is pre-written. Prisoner and Havel speak in function (fear, evasion, procedure) only; the prisoner's half-sentence must carry the shape of a name without the name.

Do not confirm before B7 that the grain is already beyond recall. B1-B6 may hold only suspicion of reach. Do not name Kel'Thuzad before B8, not even as an unnamed 'former Council man' the narration already recognizes.

Havel: on cult coin (outline). Ch7 kept him as a harried, territorial captain with route-steering and a known 'who is on your back' formation question. Pre-B5, the narration must not state his guilt; it may let Jaina notice, and file under territorial, what the reader can see in hindsight.
Lyriel is alive at close. She dies in Ch9: no foreshadowing; her perimeter competence reads as ordinary. Cyndia and Lyriel hold flanks cleanly.

The old carter, the tally-man and the newer grain-man clue stay off the active board. Do not solve them. Do not re-stage the Ch7 B6 mechanism (packaging-stage carrier layer plus body participation); the new rung is live monitoring and the death-curse.
Do not claim the whole kingdom is lost. Do not give Kel'Thuzad's exact base. Do not assert full Barov guilt. Do not claim shutting Andorhal alone could undo the spread.

VERIFIER, Jaina's cast budget: the jaw-freeze in B1 is her one spell tonight (Ch7: 'I can only do it once tonight'). After it she casts nothing: no ward in B3, no frost in the flight. In Scene 2 she senses (pressure through staff and body). That costs her, but it is not a cast. 'A faster ward might have held it' (B3/B6) is her hindsight, not an option she had. The freeze is the next payment on the cost ladder: show the cost and do not heal the hands.

VERIFIER, bite logic: the freeze stops the bite, and a man with a locked jaw cannot talk. Whatever he carries for the bite (Tam had waxed paper sewn into his collar hem, Ch4) comes off him before the cold lets go. B2's questioning starts only after that.

VERIFIER, Havel: his one formation question ('Who's on your back on a raid like this?' in shape, writer's words) lands once in B1, unremarked. It was held back from Ch7 per his voice sheet. His tell stays in where his advice points, never in his wording: no sly asides, no glint. After the curse he talks faster, says 'we' more, sweats at the collar, holds a smile too long, and reaches for shelters he owns. At the break he shouts for his route and the arrow ends it. No confession speech. The words 'coin' and 'paid' first arrive in B6, in Corin's mouth. Only Havel is on cult coin; his lads are ordinary militia.

VERIFIER: no wounds to Lyriel or Sylvanas this chapter. Ch9 owns Lyriel's death and Sylvanas's serious wound. 'A trap they barely survive' is a near miss. Lyriel's competence reads as ordinary, and she gets no wistful lines.

VERIFIER, Kel'Thuzad guardrails: in B8-B9 only the name, Kirin Tor, expelled by Antonidas for necromantic work, and somewhere east of Andorhal. No look, no voice, no Council-of-Six lecture, no Lich King, no Northrend, no Scholomance or Caer Darrow, and no Barov tie (canon has the Barovs handing him his fortress, which would assert Barov guilt). Dalaran's silence to Corin stays unexplained; neglect versus cover is not resolved. Antonidas is not made complicit. The paired sending stone stays silent (first contact is Ch9).

VERIFIER, ground and weather from Ch7 memory: the back lane behind Kett's has no street-level cover (cover is on the roofs and at the water butt and lean-to on the near corner). Cobbles are white with dust that keeps prints, and the dye-vat stink comes off Tenter Row. Warm, dry night: 'wet' means fresh residue only, never rain or damp streets. Kett's lane-side loft door has a long iron hasp.

VERIFIER, address forms: Havel says 'Ranger-General' (correct first time, never remarked on), 'my lady' or 'Lady Proudmoore' to Jaina, and 'lad' to Corin. Corin says 'Lady Proudmoore', 'Ranger-General' (carefully) and 'Captain'. Jaina calls him 'Corin'. Cyndia reports rank first, in event order, and never jokes.

povKnowsAtOpen: Andorhal's grain is being treated at the hub before shipment; the poison goes in at packaging by skilled alchemical and necromantic hands.
The city holds a living cult network, at least eight people and two layers (handlers and contaminators), not isolated saboteurs.
Corin has been useful inside the records.
Havel keeps trying to push the work back into militia routes and shelters he controls.
Sylvanas's street read and Jaina's magical read work well enough to support a same-night ambush.
Lyriel is alive and the four-woman scouting party is intact.
Jaina's sensitivity keeps them ahead of most of the crown's awareness but not ahead of grain already moving through ordinary roads.
Brask's boy / Tam-type watchers died rather than talk (collar poison); trained men here die before they betray.
Jaina can isolate the poisoned grain magic but cannot stop the final curse that turns sickness into undeath.

Sylvanas's Ch7 rooftop sighting reaches Jaina only by report and the sketch on the back of the sheet: the eight at Fenner's, the runner and his wall-crack drop, five masked men at Kett's with the crock. She did not see it.

The plan (Ch7): Cyndia on the roofs over the back lane by the chimney across from the loft; Lyriel at the Tenter Row bend; Havel's lads at the Hurdle Lane end; Sylvanas and Jaina go in; Corin knows the hasp lock and stays behind Jaina.
Jaina cannot read people (Ch6, said aloud to Sylvanas). She reads residue, wards and spells, not minds.
Jaina's private Ch6 fear: the builder was trained in Dalaran. She ran down faces and stopped at one she did not name. Corin's summer of letters to the Citadel went unanswered (Ch7).
povDoesNotKnowAtOpen: Whether a captured zealot can stay alive long enough to talk.
Whether the local cult can kill compromised members from a distance.
Whether they are still early enough to slow the spread.
Who commands the operation or where that command sits.
That Havel is on cult coin.
Whether Sylvanas was seen from Kett's window in Ch7.
mustNotBeImpliedYet: No confirmation before B7 that the grain is already beyond recall.
No naming of Kel'Thuzad before B8.
No solution of the old carter or the newer grain-man clue.
No claim that the whole kingdom is already lost.
No foreshadowing of Lyriel's Ch9 death.
No narration that resolves the face Jaina stopped at in Ch6 before Corin says the name in B8.
No Barov link to Kel'Thuzad; no Scholomance; no Lich King.
castKnowsLeavingChapter: The network can kill captured zealots with a death-curse from a distance.
Havel was cult-paid and dies when he tries to close the trap; Sylvanas killed him.
Corin stays inside the trust boundary and stays local when the party moves on.
Andorhal is a working hub; treated grain has already moved into northern Lordaeron.
Kel'Thuzad is identified as the former Kirin Tor mind behind the plague, operating east of Andorhal.
The party can detect the plague earlier than most authorities but is still behind the spread.

pov: She opens believing one live prisoner can give them the answer they need.
The capture works, but the witness dies before she can save him.
She learns that proof can still arrive too late to protect the person carrying it.
By the end, she has a name, but she loses the belief that clarity alone will keep them ahead.

beats: Sylvanas runs the ambush, the streets, and the escape with clean practical judgment.
Jaina trusts her field instincts now, even while she still treats magic as the cleaner road to certainty.
The death-curse shows how much the work depends on Sylvanas keeping danger physical and immediate.
Their coordination is fast enough to look effortless.

team.label: Partnership
beats: Their partnership is finally working at full speed.
Each woman covers the other's blind side before being asked.
They do not need speeches to show trust.
The cult answers that trust with a trap they barely survive.

castAndHandoffRules: Cyndia: still with the hunting party.
Lyriel: still with the hunting party and alive at close. She is still the one who talks to Jaina and jokes where Cyndia will not.
Corin: a real ally inside Andorhal. He stays local once the party moves on.
Captain Havel: posing as an ally at open. Exposed as a cult-paid contact and killed in the escape.
Kel'Thuzad: not yet named at chapter open.
The old carter and the newer grain-man clue: keep off the active board.
Next chapter starts: Chapter 9 opens with the same four-woman scouting party hunting east into the Eastweald.
chapterBridge: Ch7 (Sylvanas POV) closes at the militia post. 'Tonight.' The belt knife comes out of the table and the sheet curls round her sketch of Kett's crock and five strokes. Corin buckles his satchel for the hasp. Sylvanas says 'Stay behind Proudmoore' and pinches out the candle. Ch8 is back in Jaina's head for the first time since Ch6, minutes later. The walk down Hurdle Lane is done and they are in position at the back lane behind Kett's. One anchor is enough: the one cast she is holding in two bare fingertips, the dark after the candle, or the positions Sylvanas gave. Jaina knows the rooftop sighting (the runner, the five masked men, the crock) only from Sylvanas's report and the sketch. Narration says 'Sylvanas'; aloud Jaina says 'Ranger-General', and Sylvanas says 'Proudmoore' in company.

scene.title: The Capture
scene.sceneFunction: The party takes a living cultist, gets real structure out of him, and loses him to a death-curse before he can give them the name they need.
scene.knowledgeAtSceneStart: Minutes after the decision; the candle at the post is out. The target is the man who comes and goes alone through Kett's lane door. The natural fit is the runner Sylvanas sketched in Ch7 (big, going soft, brown beard, a loader's pad on one shoulder, no mask), and Jaina knows him only from her description. Positions are as Ch7 set them: Cyndia on the roofs over the back lane by the chimney across from the loft, Lyriel at the Tenter Row bend, Havel's lads at the Hurdle Lane end, Sylvanas and Jaina in, Corin behind Jaina. Havel himself is close enough to steer where the man is taken afterwards. Jaina holds one cast (the jaw-freeze); her crystal is dark, she has two bare fingertips, and her right hand is dead. The leadership is still unnamed.

beats.goal: Take a living cultist tonight, before the cell realizes it has been breached.
beats.conflict: Ch7 settled 'Tonight', so Havel's slow-procedure push is not re-argued. It survives as one last try in motion and as steering: where to carry the man, which end to leave by, a shelter of his a minute off Hurdle Lane. There are wards to smother before they flare. Jaina can read wards Sylvanas cannot see. Where they sit (the door, the lane, the man) is the writer's call, but smothering them must not spend Jaina's one cast. Corin, who came for the lock, is the natural hands at her word. Taking the man at the door risks the five upstairs, so the take happens in the lane after he leaves it, on the move. The back lane has no street-level cover. He must be taken breathing, and Jaina's fingertips must reach his jaw before he thinks to bite.

outcome.summary: They take the zealot alive and bound, and the capture is quiet, but nobody knows whether it was noticed, and Havel's lane and his offered shelter become where the man gets carried.

beats.valueShift: plan -> execution; friction-free partnership under thin cover
newOnPageInformation: The zealot is taken alive, wards smothered before they flared
Havel supplies the nearby shelter (the safe house) for questioning
Jaina and Sylvanas run a strike with no wasted movement
stillUnknownAfterBeat: Whether the prisoner knows anything useful
sensoryAnchors: dust-white cobbles in the back lane that keep every print
dye-vat sourness drifting from Tenter Row
a ward's heat she can feel and Sylvanas cannot
Lyriel and Cyndia sealing the exits
the long iron hasp on Kett's lane door
Sylvanas moving, not waiting at a door
the cold leaving her fingertip into his jaw
beats.interiority: one live man is the answer, the clean one, after a summer of sacks; she asked for one man close enough to touch and Sylvanas brought him to her; the cold in her fingertip is the last spell she has tonight and she is not counting it; Havel's shelter is the one nobody argued with
beats.transitionIntent: action-continuation: the man is bound and silent under her cold. Havel's shelter is a minute off Hurdle Lane, and the questioning has to start before the cell misses him. B2 opens in that shelter.
beats.castFunction: Sylvanas calls the take by event, not by clock. Jaina contributes the ward-read and the touch. Corin works the lock or ward at her word, then stays behind her. Cyndia and Lyriel acknowledge in a word. Havel asks his formation question once, as care, and the narration does not remark on it; Jaina hears a thorough captain. Afterwards he offers his shelter as procedure.

additionalMemoryRefs.use: back-lane geometry (no street-level cover, a lamp at each end, Kett's the last door on the left), the hasp, the dye-vat smell. Callback anchors only; do not re-describe.
the runner's look (Sylvanas's report) and the cell's trained discipline
the jaw-freeze is the next payment; her state going in (dark crystal, two white fingertips)
the collar hem Jaina saw cut open at the cage; the reason for the freeze
his steering toward lanes and shelters he controls; the formation question was held for Ch8
he knows the hasp lock and came along for it

continuityNotes: Do not re-stage Ch7's dawn-versus-tonight argument. Havel's procedure push survives as one try in motion.
The take reconciles Ch7 ('one man coming and going alone through that door') with the outline ('on the move instead of at a door'): he leaves the door and is taken in the lane.

Don't leave Jaina's Ch7 loft read dangling ('It's wet in that loft tonight... I can still read it there'). Either she gets residue off the man's skin when her fingertips land, or one clause registers that the loft is the price of taking him in the lane. Writer's choice; one clause either way.
Tam (Ch4) was Jaina's POV: she was at the cage. Callback in a clause at most; do not retell it.

Arc load: POV bullet 1 (one live prisoner is the answer); through-POV bullet 1 (Sylvanas runs the ambush); partnership bullets 1-2 (full speed, and blind sides covered before anyone asks: Jaina reads what Sylvanas can't see, and Sylvanas puts the man under Jaina's fingers).

beats.goal: Get the structure of the cell and the name of whoever is above it out of the prisoner.
beats.conflict: The man fears his masters more than his captors. Havel keeps trying to drag the questioning back to shelters, names and procedure. Sylvanas works the man with silence rather than threat, and that does most of the work. Jaina gets at least one question of her own in, of her kind (what he handles, who taught the handling), so she is not a passenger. Then she listens for the name arriving and for any magic hovering round him.

outcome.summary: They get structure: one mortal mastermind above the cell, poisoned grain planned over months, lower-rank cultists handling the infected without understanding the full ritual. The name is nearly there and does not land.

beats.valueShift: hope of a clean answer -> a name within reach
newOnPageInformation: The operation answers upward to one mortal mastermind
Poisoned grain was planned over months
Lower-rank cultists handle the infected without understanding the full ritual
The man fears his masters more than his captors
stillUnknownAfterBeat: Whether the prisoner will live to say it
sensoryAnchors: Jaina hearing the shape of a name
beats.interiority: she can almost hear the shape of the word and knows the shape matters; the collar was supposed to be the danger, and she took the jaw first; if she is fast enough this time
beats.transitionIntent: dialogue hook / planted question: the sentence is half-built and the name is a breath off. Whatever comes next arrives from outside the room.
beats.castFunction: Sylvanas keeps the man's terror pointed at his masters. Jaina asks her question and then listens for the magic, which to her is still the cleaner road. That is through-POV bullet 2: she trusts Sylvanas's field instinct with the man while still expecting the answer to come through her craft. Havel's interruptions are procedural and steer toward shelters and names. Corin is silent at the door. Lyriel and Cyndia hold the exits.

additionalMemoryRefs.use: contrast: Tam said 'I'm not to speak to you' and died; this man speaks. Do not echo Tam's line.
the face Jaina stopped at; it can flicker at the half-sentence, but the narration does not close it

continuityNotes: The structure is new on the page: one mortal mastermind, months of planning, lower ranks handling the infected without the full ritual. Keep it partial and shaded by fear. Informant scenes work when the source holds back.

The half-sentence carries the shape of a name without the name. The planner's suggestion (a title or a place of origin, never a name) stands as a suggestion. It must stay open enough that Jaina's Ch6 face can flicker without the narration closing it. The close needs Corin's knowledge in B8.
The safe house is Havel's shelter. Describe it once, here; S2 only leaves it.
Mechanism rung for Ch7-8 (plague-mechanism.md): live monitoring and handler-directed obedience. The man is the evidence of obedience; B3 is the monitoring. Do not re-stage the Ch7 grain mechanism.
Control has to shift at least once in the exchange (craft research). Without that it is a question-and-answer list.

beats.goal: Hold the man long enough for the name to come out.
beats.conflict: A necromantic death-curse arrives from outside the room and kills him mid-sentence. Jaina feels it a breath too late: a cold needle through the room, and nothing her ward could have caught from there. The speed of the response makes the room smaller and more dangerous at once, and Havel looks worse after the curse, not better.

outcome.summary: The prisoner dies before the name; the network can kill compromised zealots from a distance, and capable cult mages are working inside the city. The safe house is now known.

newOnPageInformation: A necromantic death-curse can kill a captured zealot at range
Capable cult mages operate inside the city
The cult's response was fast and exact
stillUnknownAfterBeat: How many enforcers are already moving
beats.interiority: a faster ward might have held it; she felt it and it was already finished; what she is going to remember is the half-sentence, not the man
beats.transitionIntent: action-continuation: if the cult can reach into this room, the room is already a target. Sylvanas is moving before the body settles, and S2 opens on the way out.
beats.castFunction: Sylvanas shifts from questioner to rear guard in one beat; Corin goes white; Havel's reaction is the wrong shape (he looks to the door he arrived by).

additionalMemoryRefs.use: the first captive who died before talking (poison he carried). This one is killed from outside, at a distance.
her cast is spent; she can feel the spell but has nothing left to throw at it
what Jaina can and cannot read (residue, wards; not minds)

continuityNotes: POV logic for 'felt it too late': Jaina had her fingertips on his skin in B1 and found no warning. Ch7-8 mechanism rung: the loudest signature is not the whole mechanism. Any residue he carries is loud, and something quieter can sit under it until it fires. The writer may use this; it is not required.

The evolution from Tam is reach: he carried his own death, and this man is killed from outside by a caster inside the city (investigation-arc.md). Explain the mechanism no further than Jaina can feel it.
Her cast is spent, so there is no ward here. 'A faster ward' is hindsight.

Havel after the curse shows his voice-sheet tells (faster, more 'we', sweat at the collar, a smile held too long) and a wrong-shaped look at the door he came in by. The narration notices and draws no conclusion.
Arc load: POV bullet 2 (the witness dies before she can save him). Through-POV bullet 3 begins: the danger arrives where nobody can see it, and Sylvanas makes it physical at once.

scene.verifierPacingNote: Medium weight. B1 runs fast, B2 is the longest and talkiest beat in the scene, and B3 is short and abrupt.
